rv.q: Both unsettling and unexpectedly tender, this beautifully crafted two-hander pulls the audience into its strange, delicate world and keeps us hooked from start to finish.
Excellent writing and production of a play which, at its heart, is about love, or is it?
Blink allows us to sit in the knowledge that both these things can be true.
But despite the fascinating premise and its social implications, the script falls apart slightly towards the latter half of the play, resulting in an ending that feels rushed and a bit unearned.

cn.t: Porter's quirky two-hander about lonely neighbors feels timely in its exploration of connection and isolation, though its darker parasocial undertones unsettle. Critics find it oddly poignant and beautifully crafted, if unconventional.
